title: BioMem: Agentic Memory for Biomedical LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.13426v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated considerable potential in biomedical applications, while agentic memory systems have emerged as a promising approach to preserving and utilizing information across tasks and interactions. However, a fundamental question remains: how effectively and reliably do these systems retain, retrieve, update, and utilize biomedical information? In this study, we systematically investigate agentic memory in the biomedical domain, focusing on task effectiveness, retrieval quality, information fidelity, and long-term robustness. We evaluate five memory approaches across four LLMs in three representative settings: biomedical knowledge reasoning, clinical prediction, and long-term conversational memory. Our analyses reveal how memory construction, evidence relevance, and conversational history shape downstream biomedical performance, highlighting the distinct challenges of retrieving relevant information,

translated_title: BioMem：面向生物医学大语言模型智能体的智能体记忆
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）在生物医学应用中已展现出可观的潜力，而智能体记忆系统已成为一种在任务与交互之间保存和利用信息的有前景的方法。然而，一个根本性问题仍然存在：这些系统在多大程度上能够有效且可靠地保留、检索、更新和利用生物医学信息？在本研究中，我们系统地研究了生物医学领域的智能体记忆，重点关注任务有效性、检索质量、信息保真度和长期鲁棒性。我们在三种代表性场景（生物医学知识推理、临床预测和长期对话记忆）中，对四种LLM上的五种记忆方法进行了评估。我们的分析揭示了记忆构建、证据相关性和对话历史如何影响下游生物医学性能，并突出了检索相关信息所面临的独特挑战。
tldr: 本研究提出BioMem，系统评估了生物医学领域中多种LLM智能体记忆方法在任务有效性、检索质量、信息保真度和长期鲁棒性方面的表现与挑战。
en_tdlr: This study introduces BioMem, a systematic evaluation of five agentic memory approaches for biomedical LLM agents across task effectiveness, retrieval quality, information fidelity, and long-term robustness.
